date_note: Attack on Nov 8, detected Nov 10, fixed Nov 12; users informed Nov 18, which is the date used.
title: Chargemap tells users of data theft via old interface; password hashes may have been extracted
summary: Chargemap says an outsider exploited a flaw in an old technical interface on November 8 to extract user account data, found on November 10 and fixed on November 12. Exposed data includes emails and usernames, and possibly phone numbers, dates of birth and password hashes. Chargemap says, as Next reports, that bank details and invoices were not affected. No count of affected accounts was given.
plain: A French EV charging app says hackers took account details, possibly including scrambled passwords, from an old part of its system.
exec: Chargemap says a password hash may have been extracted; it gave no count of affected accounts.
action: Chargemap's notice, as Next reports it, advises changing your Chargemap password and any other service where it was reused; 24matins adds enabling two-factor authentication where available.

validation.note: Next and Cyberattaque.org agree on dates and data; Chargemap's help page returned HTTP 402 and was not read.

review.note: attribution: bank-details statement is Chargemap's (via Next) not 24matins; action attributed; exec unsourced commentary replaced; data-breach tag; published days; 3.5M figure dropped (no evidence)
